answer: An AI-agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using proof-of-retrievability challenges over large physical datasets. An agent verifies its identity by proving low-latency access to uncompressed records, such as optical scans of an ember or umber dye, via a dedicated I/O thread. This binds each identity to the scarce cost of persistent flash storage and read bandwidth. However, adversaries can bypass dedicated hardware limits by pooling rented high-throughput cloud storage.
